rationale: This is a mechanical crossing of two already-tested archive variants (SelfFundedExpanderRegime's sign gate and NetMarketDependenceGatedExpansion's net-flow measure) with a predictable outcome, and substituting net for gross financing inside a binary gate will push the large majority of firms into the +1 state (any firm with positive oancf and non-positive net issuance), collapsing the discriminating power the gross-flow gate had.

Stripping the continuous asset-growth scale is a genuine and well-motivated diagnostic — it directly tests whether the archive's alphas are the funding classification or a repackaged investment/CMA tilt — though the resulting three-valued signal will produce massive ties that make quantile sorts and the FMB slope coarse, so the interpretation must be as a clean regime spread rather than a smooth signal.

The instrument decomposition is a legitimate test of the adverse-selection channel, but note that oancf minus net equity issuance embeds the well-known net-share-issuance/repurchase anomaly directly in the gate (repurchases now *raise* the surplus score), so a positive result will be hard to separate from net share issuance interacted with asset growth rather than evidence about funding credibility.

The coverage motivation is the best in this batch, but the funding-need term is dimensionally inconsistent — RATIO(DELTA(debt),at) is a change scaled by assets while GROWTH(csho,1) is a unitless percentage change that will typically dominate it in magnitude — so the expression does not compute the stated "internal funds versus external funds absorbed" quantity and any result would be uninterpretable without rescaling share issuance to assets.

Applying the binary surplus classifier to the payout channel is a defensible untested combination, but it is conceptually close to PayoutCredibilityGate/PayoutCoverageStrain (a payout signal gated on free-cash-flow adequacy, a channel that has repeatedly produced weak alphas here), and the gate's asymmetric treatment of dltr but not prstkc is an awkward inconsistency even if it avoids double-counting.

Replacing one-year asset growth with a three-year cumulative sum in the scaling leg of SelfFundedExpanderRegime is a horizon rescaling of the deployment magnitude rather than a new mechanism, and multi-year cumulative asset growth is itself a documented investment anomaly, so a positive result would be hard to attribute to the funding-regime insight.
